newsitem.title: GERMANY: German copper smelter sees 96/97 sales steady or up.
newsitem.headline: German copper smelter sees 96/97 sales steady or up.

text.p: Copper refiner Norddeutsche Affinerie AG (NA) said on Wednesday copper output and sales in the year to September 30, 1997 should be steady or higher than the improved figures reported for 1995/96.

"We expect to keep cathodes output at the record 368,958 tonnes reached in 95/96 and sales of copper rod and semi-fabricated products look encouraging," the chairman of the integrated smelter, Werner Marnette, told a press conference.
Cable and wire makers were ordering more copper rod as demand had picked up with improved economic conditions.
Demand from the ailing building industry was only sluggish, but NA was trying to get around the problem by developing and placing more value-added semis, which brought higher returns.
Cathode production in 95/96 was up six percent from 348,415 tonnes in 94/95.
Output of semis -- continuously-cast billets and cakes -- dropped to 109,950 from 134,541 tonnes a year earlier.
Copper rod output at NA and Deutsche Giessdraht, where NA has a one third shareholding, totalled 227,940 tonnes, up from 220,284 in 94/95.
Gold output dropped to 7.8 tonnes from 8.2 and silver declined to 131.6 tonnes from 223.8. Lead output fell to 9,566 tonnes compared with 20,178 a year earlier.
Sales of sulphuric acid, a copper by-product, rose by 7.6 percent to 656,361 tonnes, but returns were unsatisfactory.
Net profits at NA rose to 30.4 million marks in 1995/96 after 8.6 million in 94/95, on sales of 2.15 billion marks, 6.9 percent down on the year before.
Marnette said NA had cut costs and increased volume sales. He would be "very satisfied" if the same result could be achieved again in 96/97.
NA was freeing itself from its dependency on mass products for building industry purposes and had developed new niche products for electrical and air-conditioning applications.
NA is owned by Canada's Inmet Mining Corp, Australia's MIM Holdings Ltd and Germany's Degussa AG. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
